text:
angelo: Hey team — hitting an annoying issue: our iOS app starts receiving the SSE transcript then the connection drops mid-stream when the phone switches from LTE -> WiFi. We only get ~30% of the tokens, but billing shows full tokens generated. App v1.9.2. Happens frequently on carrier handoffs. Any known issues or quick workarounds?

samir: Sorry about that, can you paste the client logs around the disconnect and the request id? Also which auth flow are you using (short-lived streaming token vs API key)?

angelo: Using short-lived streaming tokens (60s TTL). Quick logs:
```
[2026-02-12T14:02:41.122Z] SSE open: req=rc_01F... seq=0
[2026-02-12T14:02:55.330Z] event: {"type":"partial","tokens":152}
[2026-02-12T14:03:03.004Z] network: switching from lte to wifi
[2026-02-12T14:03:03.210Z] connection: closed, code=0, reason="peer reset"
[2026-02-12T14:03:03.212Z] billing: charged tokens: 518
```
Not much else client-side; reconnect attempts do a fresh EventSource with new token but we still get truncated responses (sometimes 502).

nina: This reads like a keepalive/token handoff race. If the token TTL expires exactly during the handover, our streaming worker can mark the stream aborted and finish billing for produced output while the client only saw partial chunks. Two asks: 1) can you repro with network profiler (pcap) so we can see TCP FIN / RST timing, 2) if possible, capture the server-side request-id header from the response (x-rc-request-id).

angelo: I can capture a pcap and include the header. Quick question — is there any server-side grace window for token refresh during active streams?

elaine: Short answer: we currently accept tokens only at connect time, and when a token expires the worker will end the stream. We do have a 5s grace for heartbeat misses but not for auth TTL. We could: 1) extend the auth grace window for in-flight streams to ~10s, or 2) add a lightweight refresh handshake that lets an existing stream revalidate if the original client proves possession. Both have tradeoffs (longer grace increases risk if token leaked; handshake adds protocol complexity).

qa-bot: automated repro run #42 on iOS sim: reproduced. Observed sequence: CONNECT -> partial events -> token expiry at t+58s -> server sends STREAM_END (code 440) -> client sees connection close -> new connect returns fresh response but lost KV state.

nina: From ops POV, short-term mitigation: ask clients to 1) use a slightly longer streaming token TTL (e.g., 180s) for mobile handoffs or 2) send a proactive keepalive from client to avoid token expiry during the transition. Also we can patch servers to allow a one-time post-expiry revalidate if reconnection within 12s occurs and client supplies previous req id. Would that be acceptable?

samir: For support next steps: angelo, please attach the pcap + a minimal repro (we have a small node script below that mimics your flow — can you try it?):
```
// client: open stream then simulate network flip
const es = new EventSource(url + '?token=SHORT_LIVED');
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('msg', e.data);
setTimeout(() => simulateNetworkFlip(), 21000);
```
If repro matches we will escalate to eng-runtime with the server request-id and pcap.

angelo: Will run the script and attach pcap + headers. Thanks — happy to test a server-side grace patch if you want us to validate.

elaine: Thanks — we'll spin up a patch branch that accepts a 12s auth revalidate for active streams and run canary. If that looks good we'll push a config flag so customers with mobile handoffs can opt-in.

samir: Filing escalation: INC-2771 — "stream abort on mobile handoff when token TTL overlaps keepalive". Tagging eng-runtime + oncall. angelo, I'll DM for the pcap and sample. :thumbsup:

angelo: thanks all :pray:
